## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kusalacittakathā* (Kv 22.2) is a canonical debate text in the twenty-second chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, belonging to the Abhidhamma Piṭaka of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral indexes one modern translation in one language and lists no curated cross-canonical parallels [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship, the term *kusalacitta* commonly appears as a general Abhidhamma technical category denoting wholesome consciousness; in reference to Kathāvatthu debates, Nalinaksha Dutt notes that the Theravādins debated the Andhakas regarding the status of the arahant, including the claim that an arahant accumulates merit and passes away with wholesome consciousness (*kusalacitta*) [Dutt 1978].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive formulaic text reuse, showing 117 matching passages shared with 12 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The highest concentration of reuse occurs with other Kathāvatthu debates, most substantially with the *Atthiarahatopuññūpacayotikathā* (Kv 17.1, 9 matches, including a large shared block between §2.4–2.13 and §3.12–4.4), the adjacent *Āneñjakathā* (Kv 22.3, 13 matches), and the *Parihānikathā* (Kv 1.2, 10 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also shared with the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22, 7 matches), the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 8), and several other Kathāvatthu discourses (Kv 2.4, Kv 4.1, Kv 4.4, Kv 8.9, Kv 9.9, Kv 9.10, Kv 14.1) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-tradition alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with a Tibetan translation of the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra* (D0119, 5 matches) and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 26, 5 matches), though SuttaCentral records no curated parallels between them [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
